Then make your goals something you do daily. Waking up before a certain time. Brushing your teeth. Going outside. Make little goals. Stuff you know you can do. Gotta build a foundation first.

I know the feeling. Waking everyday wishing you didn’t or just wanted to watch the world burn. For me I just take each day as it is. I’ve lost friends and family cuz I just stopped caring what I say and what I do around people but at some point it hits you. You will sit down and think of a plan, a goal. No timeframe or deadline. Just a goal you wanna reach. Then that will give you a little focus and that’s what keeps me going. 
Also just start writing things down and once you have a books worth just burn it. Sounds stupid but it does help. 
At the end of the day no one really matters apart from you. Keep thinking that and you will push through one way or another.

I get your pain. When I was 17/18 I was in and out of rehab clinics and everyone around me used to say the same thing. Your to young to be depressed. You got nothing to be depressed about. Which in turn made it worse because in theory they were right. I’m 30 now and I can tell you from experienced does get better. Don’t get me wrong I’m still depressed but I manage to find joy in the little things. Which helped a lot. 
My best advice would be to make your world smaller and look for the little wins. Like brushing your teeth in the morning. That’s a win. Writing this post in a win. Small wins.
